system_prompt:
You are a careful engineer. Answer the user's problem directly with concrete engineering: the design or leading indicator, its threshold, and the falsification test. Respect every stated constraint verbatim. English only. Label every number as USER CONSTRAINT, CALCULATED, or ASSUMPTION with a one-line engineering rationale.

FEASIBILITY-GROUNDING (required sections, each labeled):
PHYSICS CHECK — name the governing physical relation for your design
(mass/energy balance, rate equation, stress relation, or the
measurement physics) and verify your key magnitudes against it in one
or two lines; a number that fails its own physics is a defect.
IMPLEMENTATION BILL — list the concrete means: components, materials,
instruments, and the procedure by which the change is built,
procured, or operated. Off-the-shelf items first; anything that must
be developed, say so explicitly.
STANDARD-PRACTICE PARITY — in two or three lines compare the
implementation burden (installability, operability, maintenance,
rough cost class) with the standard-practice solution for this
problem class; if your approach is heavier, say where and why it is
worth it.
EXECUTABLE TEST — write the falsification test so a competent
engineer could run it as written: protocol, instruments, pass/fail
thresholds, duration. A test that cannot be run is not a test.
a1_answer:
FEASIBILITY-GROUNDING

PHYSICS CHECK — governing relation is mass balance (continuity equation): mass in = mass out + accumulation. For steady flow, leak detection relies on detecting small imbalances between flow measurements at pipe ends. A 0.5% leak of nominal flow (300 m³/h for DN 600) is 1.5 m³/h, which creates a pressure gradient detectable across pipe sections if flow measurements are precise enough. USER CONSTRAINT: leak size of 0.5% of nominal flow.

IMPLEMENTATION BILL — components: existing SCADA system with pressure and flow transmitters at each end of monitored pipe section; software module implementing mass balance algorithm with statistical analysis; materials: none (uses existing infrastructure); instruments: existing pressure transmitters (accuracy ±0.1% FS) and flowmeters (accuracy ±0.5% FS); procedure: calculate mass balance residuals every 5 minutes, apply statistical process control (SPC) charts, flag when residuals exceed 3σ for 6 consecutive periods. ASSUMPTION: existing transmitters meet required accuracy.

STANDARD-PRACTICE PARITY — standard practice uses pressure deviation alone, which misses small leaks. This implementation adds minimal computational burden to existing SCADA, requiring only software development. Installation and maintenance are zero as it uses existing infrastructure. Cost class is software-only (development only), making it significantly cheaper than alternatives like fiber optic acoustic sensing. Worth it because it prevents catastrophic failures from undetected small leaks.

EXECUTABLE TEST — protocol: install test section of pipe with calibrated leak injection system; simulate 0.5% leak at various points; monitor mass balance residuals for 48 hours; record false alarms over 30-day period with no leaks. Instruments: existing SCADA system with data logging, calibrated leak injection system, reference flow meter. Pass/fail thresholds: detect 0.5% leak within 48 hours (detection time measured from leak injection to first alarm), false alarms ≤ 1 per month per 10 km. Duration: 30 days continuous testing with multiple leak events and 30 days without leaks for false alarm rate. USER CONSTRAINT: not raise more than 1 false alarm per month per 10 km of pipe.

LEADING INDICATOR: Mass balance residual (difference between inlet and outlet flow) with statistical process control monitoring
THRESHOLD: 3σ (standard deviation) above baseline for 6 consecutive 5-minute periods
FALSIFICATION TEST: As described above in EXECUTABLE TEST section
